connector: Last time you polished your writing. Today you write about yourself as a reader. Who were you in August, and who are you now? Bring proof, the way you would for a character.

a.raw: put this packet underneath do you understand hurry
a.fixed: “Put this packet underneath; do you understand? Hurry.”
a.why: Mama’s real words in Number the Stars: three short pieces, each with its own mark, inside one pair of quotation marks.

b.raw: in august i read slowly but now i read with a pencil in my hand
b.fixed: In August I read slowly, but now I read with a pencil in my hand.
b.why: Capitals on In, August and I; a comma before but joins two complete thoughts; a period ends it.

scholar.journal-q1: … and name a book from the start and one from the end.
scholar.journal-q3: … and name who should NOT read it, too.

fields.label: Me as a reader in August

notes.wgrd: Reflect on how your reading habits have grown: who you were as a reader in August, who you are now, and the proof.
vocab: To change your writing to make the ideas better.
To check writing for mistakes in capitals, usage, punctuation and spelling.
A collection of your best work.
To think back on something and what it taught you.
notes.wordParts: Every base from the year: port, tract, struct, spect, ject, script, rupt, duct, form, press, tain, lev, plus prefixes like pre-, re-, trans-, inter-.
notes.grammar: Spiral review: capitals, commas, quotation marks, complete sentences. Read your sentence out loud and check each mark has a job.
notes.spelling: Spiral review: drop the silent e, change y to i, double the last consonant when the beat is on the last syllable, and spell each word part the same way every time.

transcripts.welcome: Hoo, hello! It’s Opti. Today you write about yourself as a reader. Today’s question: who were you as a reader in August, and who are you now?
transcripts.read: Think about the first book this year and the last. What can you do now that you couldn’t do then? Name the skill. Then prove it, the way you’d prove something about a character, with a real example.
transcripts.grammar: Proofread like an editor. Read slowly, one sentence at a time. Check capitals, then usage, then punctuation, then spelling. Four quick passes catch more than one long one.
